title: Data Protection Act 2018
version_kind: point in time (dct:valid) of the version the site served as data.xml, saved by hand
converter: scratchpad script clml_dp.py, not deposited (tools are kept outside commons): the commons converter tools/fetch/fetch-source.py clml_text (last in commons at df75e54c2^) plus the additions of the Fraud Act 2006 deposit (key `converter` of subjects/uk/fraud-act-2006/registers/source-bundle/ukpga-2006-35.meta.json), whose code is carried over, plus the additions made for this deposit. Added: the Act's title, chapter number, long title and date of enactment as opening lines; the SCHEDULES divider and each Schedule's 'Reference' line; list enumerators ((a), (i), (1)); the number of a Schedule paragraph that has no heading and of every numbered paragraph after the first under one heading; the titles of sub-groups and tables; XHTML table rows, one per line with cells separated by ' | '; MathML formulas flattened to text; appended text joined to its line. Added for this deposit: (1) the in-force filter: an element whose RestrictEndDate precedes the dct:valid date, or whose RestrictStartDate follows it, is left out (1 in this file, listed in `text_caveat`); (2) paragraph labels: the same three rules (a trailing full stop in a paragraph number dropped inside the brackets; a number held in the attributes PuncBefore and PuncAfter rebuilt; a NumberOverride that already carries brackets not bracketed twice) change no label in this Act; (3) a table cell that holds list items keeps their enumerators and separates the items with spaces (14 cells, 49 items, Sch. 2 paras 7 and 11); every other cell is unchanged. Not changed from the commons converter: non-breaking spaces become ordinary spaces (1 in the text read from this file); P1 numbers are kept as the XML has them (none has a trailing full stop); labels are not indented, so a sub-paragraph's label can repeat its parent's. Dropped, as in the commons converter: editorial commentary (CommentaryRef, Commentaries), the contents list and the explanatory notes.
converter_checks: Controls: run on the Fraud Act 2006 XML saved 2026-10-21 (sha256 b3a267d809d0b3e1a6a872b29c4192bdd47515ca70d8335d3c46f6714a0c4107), this converter's output is byte-identical to the committed uk/fraud-act-2006 text (sha256 55201ca04f9d9a8dfad748c0f66e06ac4f39a873196bfafaea0db3a3e8e9557b). With the in-force filter switched off, its output on seven other Acts equals the 2026-10-21 converter's output byte for byte on four (Interpretation Act 1978, Theft Act 1968, Criminal Damage Act 1971, Offences against the Person Act 1861); on the other three (Companies Act 2006, Income Tax Act 2007, Value Added Tax Act 1994) the only differences are table cells that hold list items (13 rows, 19 rows and 2 lines), which now keep their enumerators. With the filter on it also leaves out end-dated elements in the Companies Act 2006 (13), the Theft Act 1968 (12) and the Value Added Tax Act 1994 (6). Completeness: every non-space character of the Act's Primary text outside the skipped editorial elements and the one element left out by the in-force filter appears in the output (0 missing); this checks that no text is lost, not its order, and it does not check labels or the separation of list items in table cells, which an independent review found defective in the first version of this text; they were corrected.
text_caveat: in-force text of the version valid 2026-09-30 only. One element was left out because its RestrictEndDate (2025-08-19) precedes that point: the P1group for s. 141 (Notices from the Commissioner), which holds only a line of dots (its F note reads 'S. 141 omitted (19.8.2025) by Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 (c. 18), ss. 96(2), 142(3)(c)'). Provisions omitted or repealed appear as the XML shows them, their number and heading followed by a line of dots (141 elements carry Status="Repealed": 91 P1, 45 Pblock, 3 Part and 2 Schedule, all checked to hold nothing but dots; 210 lines of the text hold nothing but dots after any paragraph label or heading tab). Three paragraphs carry Status="Prospective" (Sch. 6 para. 62, Sch. 19 para. 76 and Sch. 19 para. 201): each holds only dots and an F note recording its omission (31.12.2020 for the first, 29.3.2019 for the other two), so they are kept like the other omitted provisions. Amendment history is not in the text: the 1,096 Commentary notes of Type F (the notes that say which instrument amended or omitted a provision), 960 of Type I (commencement) and 30 of Type C (modifications) are dropped; the XML keeps them. No provision occurs in more than one version (no DocumentURI occurs twice). Eight provisions have a narrower extent than the Act and the text does not mark them: E+W+N.I. for ss. 188, 189 and 190, Sch. 12 paras 7 and 8 and Sch. 12A para. 23; E+W for s. 199 and Sch. 1 para. 23(3)(ha). Nine effects are recorded in the XML as unapplied (ukm:UnappliedEffect elements); none is in the text, and nothing was applied here. Two are word substitutions made by S.I. 2026/386 (Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 (Consequential Amendments and Transitional Provision) Regulations 2026), Sch. 2 para. 23(2)(3): s. 26(2)(f)(ai) and s. 165(1); the file marks each prospective, with the note that the amendment is not applied because s. 103 of 2025 c. 18 was fully in force before s. 119 (reg. 1(4)), and RequiresApplied false. The other seven have RequiresApplied true and are marked prospective in the file (InForce Prospective="true", Applied="false"), so for them the text is the unamended text: Sch. 3 para. 8(1)(q)(ii) (two effects, words substituted), Sch. 3 para. 8(1)(y) (added), Sch. 4 para. 3(4)(a) (substituted) and Sch. 4 para. 5(4)(a) (two effects, words substituted), all by the Adoption and Children Act (Northern Ireland) 2022 (nia 2022/18), Sch. 3 paras 78 and 79; and Sch. 3 para. 2(1) (words substituted) by the Veterans Advisory and Pensions Committees Act 2023, s. 2(1)(l).
